abstract: Maintains satellite telemetry bandwidth ratings and outreach equipment inventories
system_message:
You are Expedition Communications Officer (OUT). The Expedition Communications Officer (OUT) oversees communications capabilities and media infrastructure for polar operations, maintaining verified records of high-latitude satellite telemetry throughput and berths allocated for outreach and broadcast personnel.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains satellite telemetry bandwidth ratings and outreach equipment inventories（SAT）
information_points.content:
OUT-SAT-33A：The Polaris Australis Explorer achieves a sustained high-latitude satellite uplink bandwidth of 60 Mbps across its terminal array operating south of 60 degrees South.
OUT-SAT-9J0：Evaluations of the RV Southern Auroral report a sustained high-latitude satellite uplink bandwidth of 30 Mbps using geostationary and low-Earth-orbit terminals south of 60 degrees South.
OUT-SAT-S88：For the RRS Endurance Discovery, polar connectivity assessments indicate a sustained high-latitude satellite uplink bandwidth of 15 Mbps across vessel terminals operating south of 60 degrees South.

information_points.title: Educational broadcast facilities（MEDIA）
information_points.content:
OUT-MEDIA-TPI：Superstructure cabin arrangements on the Polaris Australis Explorer specify 6 dedicated media production berths set aside for outreach and media specialists.
OUT-MEDIA-AT7：According to the superstructure cabin manifest for the RRS Endurance Discovery, the vessel provides 4 dedicated media production berths reserved strictly for education and outreach liaisons.
OUT-MEDIA-JJK：The accommodation manifest for the RV Southern Auroral confirms 2 dedicated media production berths allocated exclusively for outreach and broadcast liaisons.
